senses.def: the work or study of using science to design and build machines, structures, and systems
examples: He has a degree in mechanical engineering from Purdue.
The bridge is a remarkable piece of engineering.

senses.def: to improve the quality, value, or strength of something
examples: A fresh coat of paint can enhance the value of your home.
The new lighting enhances the colors of the paintings.

note: Used for making good things better (enhance a reputation), not for repairing something bad.

senses.def: to get pleasure from something
examples: I really enjoy cooking for friends on the weekend.
Did you enjoy the concert last night?

senses.def: to have something good, such as a right or advantage (formal)
examples: The region enjoys a mild climate all year round.

note: Enjoy needs an object or reflexive: "enjoy yourself" (NOT "I enjoyed" alone). Followed by -ing: enjoy swimming.

senses.def: giving pleasure
examples: We had a very enjoyable evening at the lake.
The hike was long but surprisingly enjoyable.

senses.def: extremely large in size, amount, or degree
examples: They live in an enormous house with seven bedrooms.
The project was an enormous success.

note: "Enormity" usually means the great seriousness of something bad, not just large size.

senses.def: as much or as many as you need or want
examples: We don't have enough chairs for everyone.
Is there enough time to grab a coffee?

senses.def: to the necessary degree (placed after an adjective, adverb, or verb)
examples: He isn't old enough to drive.
You're not studying hard enough.

senses.def: a sufficient amount, or as much as you can accept
examples: I've had enough of your excuses.
Thanks, that's enough for me.

note: Word order trap: enough + noun (enough money), but adjective + enough (big enough), never "enough big".

senses.def: to ask someone for information (formal)
examples: Several customers called to enquire about the delay.
I'm writing to enquire whether the position is still open.

note: Mainly British spelling. American English almost always uses "inquire".

senses.def: a question you ask in order to get information
examples: We received hundreds of enquiries about the job.

senses.def: an official investigation into the cause of something
examples: The government has ordered an enquiry into the hospital deaths.

note: Mainly British spelling; Americans write "inquiry" (pronounced /ˈɪŋkwəri/ or /ɪnˈkwaɪəri/).

senses.def: to improve the quality of something, often by adding something to it
examples: Traveling abroad really enriched my life.
The cereal is enriched with iron and vitamins.

senses.def: to make someone richer, often unfairly
examples: Critics say the deal only enriched a few insiders.

senses.def: to officially join a course, school, or program, or to arrange for someone to join
examples: She enrolled in a night class to learn Spanish.
More than 2,000 students are enrolled at the college.

note: American spelling: enroll, enrollment; British: enrol, enrolment. Americans say "enroll in" a course.

senses.def: to happen after something or as a result of it (formal)
examples: The referee made a bad call, and a fight ensued.
In the ensuing chaos, several people were injured.

note: Formal. Usually intransitive and often in the form "the ensuing + noun".

senses.tr: sağlamak, garanti etmek, güvence altına almak
senses.def: to make certain that something happens or is true
examples: Please ensure that all windows are closed before you leave.
The new rules ensure equal pay for equal work.

note: Don't confuse with "insure" (sigortalamak) and "assure" (birine güvence vermek: assure someone that...).

senses.def: to come or go into a place
examples: Everyone stood up when the judge entered the room.
Thieves entered the house through a back window.

senses.def: to type or write information into a computer or form
examples: Enter your password and click "Log in".

senses.def: to take part in a competition, or to begin a job, period, or activity
examples: She entered the race at the last minute.
The war has entered its third year.

note: No preposition after enter for places: enter the room (NOT enter to/into the room). But "enter into" an agreement or discussion.

senses.def: a company or business
examples: The program offers loans to small and medium-sized enterprises.
The software is designed for large enterprises.

senses.def: a large or difficult project, especially a new one
examples: Building the railroad was a huge and risky enterprise.

senses.def: the ability to think of new projects and the energy to make them succeed
examples: The town's revival owes a lot to local enterprise.

senses.def: to interest or amuse people in order to give them pleasure
examples: A clown was hired to entertain the kids at the party.
The show aims to entertain as well as educate.

senses.def: to invite people to your home and give them food and drink
examples: They love to entertain, so their house is always full of guests.

senses.tr: (fikir, ihtimal) aklından geçirmek, göz önünde bulundurmak
senses.def: to consider an idea or possibility (formal)
examples: I never entertained the idea of quitting.

senses.def: enjoyable and interesting to watch, read, or listen to
examples: The movie is silly but very entertaining.
He's an entertaining storyteller who always makes us laugh.

senses.def: movies, music, shows, games, etc. that people enjoy, or the business that produces them
examples: There's live entertainment at the hotel every Friday night.
She works in the entertainment industry in Los Angeles.

senses.def: a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something
examples: The new coach brought energy and enthusiasm to the team.
She talked about her trip with great enthusiasm.

senses.def: a person who is very interested in an activity or subject and spends a lot of time on it
examples: The museum is popular with railroad enthusiasts.
He's a keen fitness enthusiast who runs every morning.

note: Informal American alternatives: "buff" (a history buff), "junkie", "nut".

senses.def: feeling or showing a lot of excitement and interest
examples: The kids were very enthusiastic about the camping trip.
The band got an enthusiastic welcome from the crowd.

note: Use "enthusiastic about" (NOT for/on).

senses.def: including every part, person, or thing; whole
examples: I spent the entire weekend cleaning the garage.
The entire town came out to watch the parade.

note: Used before a noun, usually with the/my/an: the entire team. "In its entirety" = as a whole.

senses.def: completely; in every way
examples: The meal was made entirely from local ingredients.
I'm not entirely sure what she meant.

note: "Not entirely" is a polite way to say "partly not": I'm not entirely convinced.

senses.def: to give someone the right to have or do something
examples: Full-time staff are entitled to four weeks of paid vacation.
This ticket entitles you to a free drink.

senses.def: to give a title to a book, movie, etc.
examples: Her first novel was entitled "The Long Road Home".

note: Mostly passive: be entitled to (something / do something). "Entitled" as an adjective can also mean spoiled, believing you deserve special treatment.

senses.def: something that exists separately and has its own identity, such as an organization
examples: After the merger, the two banks became a single entity.
The company operates as a separate legal entity.

note: Formal and academic; common in law and business.

senses.def: a door, gate, or passage that you use to enter a place
examples: Meet me at the main entrance of the museum.
The building has a separate entrance for deliveries.

senses.def: the right to go into a place or join a group; the act of coming into a room or onto a stage
examples: She passed the entrance exam for law school.
The actor made a dramatic entrance in the second act.

note: Opposite: exit. "Entrance exam" = giriş sınavı.

senses.def: a person who starts and runs businesses, especially when this involves financial risk
examples: The young entrepreneur launched her first company at 22.
The city offers grants to help local entrepreneurs.

note: Tricky spelling from French: entre-pre-neur.

senses.def: the act of going into a place, or the right to go in
examples: The thieves gained entry through an open window.
He was refused entry to the country because his visa had expired.

senses.def: a separate item in a diary, list, dictionary, or database
examples: The dictionary has over 50,000 entries.
Her last diary entry was dated June 3.

senses.def: something you submit in a competition
examples: The winning entry will be published in the magazine.

note: "Entry-level" = for beginners, with no experience needed (giriş seviyesi).

senses.def: a flat paper cover that you put a letter or card in before sending it
examples: She sealed the envelope and put a stamp on it.
The check arrived in a brown envelope.

note: "Push the envelope" = to go beyond normal limits. Don't confuse with the verb "envelop" /ɪnˈveləp/ (sarmak, kuşatmak).

senses.def: the natural world of land, water, air, plants, and animals
examples: Plastic waste is causing serious damage to the environment.
We need to protect the environment for future generations.

senses.def: the conditions and surroundings that affect how people live or work
examples: Children need a safe and loving environment to grow up in.
It's a fast-paced work environment.

note: In the "nature" sense it takes "the": damage the environment. Note the spelling: enviro-n-ment.

senses.def: connected with the natural world and its protection, or with surrounding conditions
examples: The new airport could have a serious environmental impact.
She joined an environmental group that cleans up local rivers.

note: "Environmentally friendly" = çevre dostu.

senses.def: a large number of cases of a disease in one community at the same time
examples: A flu epidemic closed schools across the state.
Health officials warned of a cholera epidemic after the floods.

senses.def: a sudden, fast increase in something bad
examples: Doctors are worried about the obesity epidemic among children.

note: Epidemic = in one area or country; pandemic = across the world.

senses.def: one part of a TV or radio series, or a podcast
examples: I stayed up late to watch the final episode of the season.
New episodes come out every Tuesday.

senses.def: a single event or short period that is important or unusual
examples: It was an embarrassing episode that he'd rather forget.
She had another episode of severe depression last year.

senses.def: the same in size, number, value, or rights as something or someone else
examples: Cut the cake into eight equal pieces.
Women and men should get equal pay for the same job.

senses.def: a person or thing with the same ability, rank, or rights as another
examples: She treats her employees as equals.
As a pianist, he had no equal.

senses.def: to be the same in amount or value as something, or to be as good as something
examples: Two plus three equals five.
Her time equaled the world record.

note: American spelling: equaled, equaling (British: equalled). "Be equal to a task" = be able to do it.

senses.def: the state of having the same rights, status, and opportunities as others
examples: The movement fought for racial equality in the 1960s.
Gender equality in the workplace is still a long way off.

senses.def: to the same degree or amount
examples: Both candidates are equally qualified for the job.
The prize money will be shared equally among the winners.

senses.def: used to add a second point that is as important as the first
examples: Exercise is important; equally, you need enough sleep.

note: Avoid "equally as": say "equally important" or "just as important".

senses.def: to think that one thing is the same as or closely linked to another
examples: Many people equate success with making a lot of money.
You can't equate criticism with disloyalty.

senses.def: to be equal to something in amount or value (equate to)
examples: The pay rise equates to about $50 a week.

note: Pattern: equate A with B. The idea is often criticized: "don't equate X with Y".

senses.def: a mathematical statement showing that two amounts are equal, such as 2x + 3 = 7
examples: The students had to solve five equations in ten minutes.
Einstein's famous equation links energy and mass.

senses.def: a situation in which several things must be considered together
examples: When you add children to the equation, moving abroad gets complicated.

collocations: the other side of the equation

senses.def: to provide someone or something with the tools or things needed for a purpose
examples: All police cars are equipped with cameras.
The gym is fully equipped with modern machines.

senses.def: to give someone the skills or knowledge they need
examples: The course equips students to work in the tech industry.

note: The p doubles: equipped, equipping.

senses.def: the tools, machines, or other things needed for a particular activity
examples: The hospital needs new medical equipment.
We rented all our camping equipment from a local store.

note: Uncountable: NOT "equipments" or "an equipment". Say "a piece of equipment".

senses.def: equal in value, amount, meaning, or importance
examples: The fine is equivalent to a month's salary.
Is there an equivalent word in Turkish?

senses.def: something that has the same value, purpose, or meaning as something else
examples: A tablespoon is the equivalent of three teaspoons.
He drank the equivalent of ten cups of coffee.

note: "Equivalent to" (adjective) vs. "the equivalent of" (noun).

senses.def: a period of history with particular features or events
examples: The fall of the Berlin Wall marked the end of an era.
We live in the era of social media.

note: "Usher in a new era" = to start a new period.

senses.def: to build something or put something in an upright position (formal)
examples: The town erected a statue in honor of the fallen soldiers.
Police erected barriers along the parade route.

senses.def: standing or sitting straight up
examples: The soldier stood erect as the flag was raised.

note: Formal; in everyday speech use "put up" or "build".

senses.def: to gradually wear away rock, soil, etc. by wind, water, or ice, or to be worn away
examples: The waves have eroded the cliffs over thousands of years.
Without trees, the soil quickly erodes.

senses.def: to gradually weaken or destroy something such as trust, power, or value
examples: The scandal has eroded public trust in the police.
Inflation is eroding people's savings.

senses.def: a mistake, especially one that causes problems or affects a result
examples: The crash was caused by human error.
There's an error in the second paragraph of your report.

note: More formal than "mistake". "Make an error" (NOT do an error). "Trial and error" = deneme yanılma.

senses.def: when a volcano erupts, it suddenly throws out fire, rocks, smoke, and lava
examples: The volcano erupted for the first time in 40 years.

senses.def: to start suddenly and violently or loudly
examples: Fighting erupted between rival gangs downtown.
The crowd erupted in cheers when the goal was scored.

senses.def: to become or make something worse, more serious, or more intense
examples: The argument quickly escalated into a fistfight.
Both sides are trying not to escalate the conflict.

senses.def: to rise rapidly in amount or cost
examples: Healthcare costs continue to escalate.

note: "Escalate an issue" in workplaces means to pass a problem to a higher manager.

senses.def: to get away from a place where you are kept against your will or from danger
examples: Two prisoners escaped from the jail overnight.
The family escaped the fire through a window.

senses.tr: (kötü bir şeyden) kurtulmak, yakayı sıyırmak; gözden kaçmak
senses.def: to avoid something bad, or to not be noticed or remembered
examples: The driver escaped serious injury.
Her name escapes me right now.

senses.def: the act of escaping, or something that helps you forget daily life
examples: The prisoner's escape made national news.
For me, reading is an escape from stress.

note: "A narrow escape" = kıl payı kurtuluş. "His name escapes me" = I can't remember it.

senses.def: more than usual or more than others; particularly
examples: I love fruit, especially strawberries.
Driving is dangerous here, especially at night.

senses.def: for a particular purpose or person
examples: I made this cake especially for you.

note: Position: usually right before the word it highlights (especially at night). "Specially" is mainly used for purpose: specially designed.

senses.def: a short piece of writing on a subject, especially one written by a student
examples: The professor asked us to write a 2,000-word essay on the Civil War.
Her college application essay was about her grandmother.

note: In US universities, students often say "paper" instead of essay.

senses.def: the most important quality of something that makes it what it is
examples: The essence of good teaching is listening to students.
In essence, the plan is to cut costs by 20 percent.

senses.def: a strong liquid taken from a plant and used for its flavor or smell
examples: Add a few drops of vanilla essence to the batter.

note: "Time is of the essence" = time is extremely important; we must hurry. Americans usually say "vanilla extract".
